explanation: Turkey's Directorate of Religious Affairs (Diyanet) has publicly discouraged eating with the left hand on religious grounds, and many Turks favor the right hand for bread and shared dishes. But a 2018 Diyanet statement calling left-handed eaters 'demons' sparked public mockery and criticism, showing the custom is more contested than the stronger taboo seen in Gulf countries, and secular/urban Turks follow it less strictly.
local_tip: Use your right hand for shared dishes and bread to be safe, but don't worry about it if you're left-handed eating your own plate in casual, secular settings.
regional_note: The custom is observed most strictly in religious and rural households and is often relaxed in secular, urban circles.

also_check.note: The left hand is considered unclean and reserved for bathroom use; eat with the right hand.
No strong taboo against the left hand; chopstick etiquette matters far more.
Eating with the left hand is also considered unclean; use the right hand, especially from communal dishes.
